subject: Governance deployment annex and evaluation process for Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Rachel Meyers <rachel.m@aurorafinance.com>

Cc: Aurora Finance Procurement <procurement@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: governance annex + evidence for RFP (NIST / EU AI Act alignment)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Aurora product team was impressed with Redwood's latency and cost controls. Our procurement and compliance leads have opened an RFQ thread focused on governance and operational evidence. Can you send a deployment annex that describes:

- How Redwood maps to the NIST AI RMF core functions (Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover) for hosted and private deployments.
- Evidence you can provide for model evaluation and regression (sampling approach, test corpus handling, frequency of regression runs, and versioned eval artifacts).
- EU AI Act positioning for high-risk use cases and what controls you surface for audit (model cards, traceability, documentation, human oversight points).
- Data retention and audit-log retention windows (we have a 7-year requirement for certain transactions).

We'd like the annex plus any representative eval report or template you can share by the end of next week (target 9/3). Procurement will need a short summary we can attach to our vendor package.

Attached: Aurora_RFQ_Governance_Annex_Request.docx (the RFQ worksheet).

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Meyers
Head of Vendor Risk, Aurora Finance

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: proposed content for Aurora annex (draft bullets)

Team — putting a consolidated set of bullets below that we can turn into the Annex PDF. I'm keeping the language vendor-friendly but audit-ready. Please edit inline in the Drive folder before I assemble the final PDF.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary bullets):
   - Identify: asset inventory (model_id, model_version, training_date), owner registry, data lineage tracked per request.
   - Protect: role-based access, KMS/HSM integration for keys, network isolation options (hosted vs private).
   - Detect: model drift detectors (statistical tests on embeddings + output distribution monitors), anomaly alerts exported to SIEM.
   - Respond: incident playbooks, model rollback by pinned model version, canary routing to safe fallback variants.
   - Recover: backup of model artifacts, KV cache snapshotting, post-incident re-eval and retest gating.

2) EU AI Act positioning (high-level):
   - We classify most retrieval-augmented generation and sensitive-decision flows as "high-risk" only when the customer designates a regulated decision pathway; Redwood provides controls that allow customers to meet Act obligations (technical documentation, traceability logs, human oversight configuration, and conformity assessment support).
   - Deliverables: model card, system-level documentation, sample traceability export (request_id -> model_version -> prompt + structured outputs).

3) Eval & regression approach (what to include):
   - Regression cadence: weekly automated smoke suite against a curated seed of prompts; monthly full-sampling regression for production models; ad-hoc regression on model version changes or architecture updates.
   - Sampling strategy: stratified sampling of prompt classes by intent + sensitivity labels; include edge-case amplification testing and adversarial prompt seeds where applicable.
   - Artifacts: versioned eval reports (PDF), diffed model metrics, audio/video logs (if applicable), and failing prompt sets.
   - Evidence for audits: test harness exports, random-seed provenance, checksum of model artifacts, and test-suite run IDs.

4) Data & audit-log retention options:
   - Default: 365 days request audit logs, 90 days prompt content retention for hosted API (configurable).
   - Enterprise option: configurable retention up to 7 years in Private deployment, extra-cost for long-term cold storage and encrypted archival.

5) Practical asks for Aurora:
   - Confirm whether you expect Redwood to be the model owner for "conformity" artifacts or whether Aurora will be the system owner (this changes who signs off on change controls).
   - Provide a short list of 3 representative PII / regulated workflows so we can flag additional controls.

Attachments we should include in outbound: evaluation-report-sample.pdf, model-card-template.md, and final Annex PDF.

Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Governance Deployment Annex + sample eval — Redwood → Aurora

Rachel — attached is the Governance Deployment Annex tailored for Aurora and a representative eval report. Key highlights below; full content attached.

Attachments: Redwood_Governance_Annex_Aurora_20260902.pdf (Governance deployment annex), evaluation-report-sample.pdf (example report)

Summary (top-line):
- NIST AI RMF: we provide artifact mappings for Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover for both Hosted and Private modes (see Annex §2.1).
- EU AI Act: Annex §3.2 describes how customers can exercise system-owner responsibilities; Redwood provides model cards, traceability exports, and human-in-the-loop hooks necessary for conformity assessments.
- Regression & eval: weekly smoke tests + monthly stratified full-sample regression; we version eval artifacts and store run metadata and checksums for auditability.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 365/90 (logs/content). For Aurora's 7-year requirement we propose Private deployment with archival retention; Annex §5 outlines cost and SLA implications.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm whether Aurora will be system-owner for conformity artifacts or if Redwood should accept delegated responsibilities (this affects access and sign-off).
2) If you want, schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Monica and Jonas to go through sample exports and the regression sampling strategy.

Proposed availability for walkthrough: Mon 9/6 10-11am PT or Tue 9/7 2-3pm PT.

Jonas and Monica — please note I attached the sample eval and the final Annex PDF. I included the Drive link for the working documents: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-redwood-aurora-governance

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
